title: Patch apply fallback notes and mini-playbook
content:
Context / why I sketched this down:
- Working through brittle ‘patch apply’ behaviour when dependent PRs land out-of-order. We have a handful of incidents where a follow-up PR assumes a patch applied cleanly but earlier migration/asset changes weren’t present and CI either flaked or merged invalid state.

Problem statement:
- Patch apply path (apply, staged-apply, commit) has multiple implicit assumptions: schema/migrations present, kv-prefixes populated, and binary ops for model artifacts. When any assumption fails, downstream PRs either fail CI or silently pass but break runtime.

High-level hypotheses:
1) Failure rate correlates with number of cross-repo deps in the change set (esp infra + migrations).
2) A simple fallback (auto-revert or auto-skip with a retriggerable job) will reduce time-to-recovery vs manual revert.
3) Lightweight pre-checks (dry-run apply + hash compare) catch ~70% of cases.

Quick experiment ideas:
- Canary runner: A nightly job that performs a dry-run patch-apply for any queued migration/infra PRs and posts results to a dedicated Slack channel. Track false positives. (INF-3120).
- PR bot enhancement: When a PR depends-on another PR, add a gating check that verifies the target commit is present in the canary pool. If not, mark as blocked and suggest rebase/hold.
- Fallback job: If apply fails during merge-time, automatically create a revert PR and label original PR with "needs-replay"; include instructions to re-run patch apply after dependency fixes.

Minimal playbook for on-call (first 30 minutes):
- If patch-apply failure alert hits: 1) Identify PR(s) involved (link in alert), 2) Run local dry-run: ./scripts/patch-apply --dry-run --pr <num>, 3) Check for migration/version mismatch in logs (look for 'missing column' / 'artifact not found'), 4) If missing dependency found, post following template to PR and slack: "Blocked: needs <PR#>. Suggested action: hold merge until dependency merges and then rebase."
- If CI passed but system errors: revert using quick revert PR template and mark incident for postmortem.

PR checklist (for authors touching patch apply / migrations):
- [ ] Add "depends-on: #<PR>" if this PR requires another repo/PR to land first
- [ ] Add a dry-run script in ./scripts/ that verifies apply on a dev-level dataset (no secrets)
- [ ] Include migration forward/backward commands in PR description
- [ ] Add an automated test stub that runs patch-apply --dry-run in CI (flake-tolerant, 2 retries)
- [ ] Document binary artifact shas in release notes if applicable

Rollback / revert heuristics (to avoid cascading failures):
- If the failure is due to missing runtime artifact: revert the PR that introduced the runtime expectation first (fast revert PR + deploy).
- If failure is due to data migration mismatch that blocks reads: consider a feature-flag rollback path for the new code path, then revert the migration PR if needed.
- For multi-repo correlated failures: prefer coordinated revert (open revert PRs in all repos and assign a single owner).

Notes from debug session on 2024-09-28:
- Observed: patch-apply returned non-zero but CI continued because a downstream job swallowed the exit code (GH action bug). Need to make the step 'fail-fast'.
- Observed: KV cache prefix missing caused silent degradation (no explicit error) — add explicit fail when required prefix not found.

Open questions / followups:
- What is the expected SLA for automated reverts? (ops cost vs risk of degraded state)
- Where should the canary dry-run results be stored (DB rows vs a burndown GitHub issue)?
- How to surface cross-repo depends-on metadata so tooling can auto-block? (Git submodule-esque metadata or comment parsing?)

Commands / snippets to copy-paste:
- local dry-run: ./scripts/patch-apply --dry-run --pr 8421 --workspace=staging
- force revert template: gh pr create --title "revert: <PR#>" --body "auto-revert due to failed patch-apply" --label revert

Short-term next actions (owner tags):
- Miriam: prototype canary dry-run job (k8s CronJob) and push to infra-sandbox (ETA 1 week)
- Carlos: add fail-fast enforcement in GH action that runs 'patch-apply' (ETA 3 days)
- Nina: draft PR template for auto-reverts + labels (ETA 4 days)

Misc scribbles (notes-to-self):
- Consider 'apply idempotence' test harness to simulate partial applies and replays.
- Capture examples of previous incidents (link them here) for dataset of failure modes.
- Maybe call this pattern "staged-apply with explicit dep metadata" in docs.

End-of-note.

Latest quick add (2025-02-06): Added a short YAML schema idea for depends-on metadata to include in PR body so bots can parse reliably. Put a TODO to wire to the PR-bot.
